headline: Your final height
subhead: IS DECIDED BY ONE CELL TYPE
body: A thin layer of stem cells sitting at the very top of the growth plate.
punch: Everything below them is just the assembly line they feed.

headline: They're called
body: The name is misleading. They aren't resting — they're the reserve. They divide slowly, and each division produces the columns of chondrocytes that actually lengthen the bone.
punch: They aren't idle. They're being spent.

headline: And they run out
body: In rabbits, over 95% of resting zone cells were dividing at birth. By 17 weeks that had collapsed to under 10%. The cell count dropped too — not just the activity.
punch: The reserve depletes both ways: fewer cells, and less active.

headline: We now know
body: They're marked by PTHrP, and single-cell sequencing of human pubertal growth plate biopsies confirmed the same two subpopulations exist in people, not just mice.
punch: This stopped being a mouse story in 2025.

headline: Activate them
body: A single Hedgehog-agonist bead implanted in one rat femur produced measurable, progressively increasing leg length versus the untreated leg on the same animal.
punch: Same animal. Same genetics. One leg longer.

headline: They also need
body: These cells only stay stem-like in a low-Wnt environment. Force canonical Wnt signalling on and they lose the ability to form columns at all.
punch: The niche isn't background. It's a requirement.

headline: And growth hormone
body: GH stimulates human resting zone cells through JAK/STAT and local TGF-beta — independent of the liver IGF-1 pathway everyone talks about.
punch: The GH story has a second half nobody covers.

headline: But here's the gap
body: Whether normal fusion is these cells clonally exhausting themselves has never been directly tested. It's the best model available and it's still inference.
punch: Best available explanation is not the same as demonstrated.

headline: It's never over
body: Real mechanisms, real citations, no protocols.
